title: Design System: Predictive Maintenance Control Center

components.name: Metric strip
components.description: Authored metric treatment; actual label/value layout is supplied by Streamlit.

components.name: Readable caption
components.description: Full-opacity caveat treatment; native typography is framework-owned.
components.html: Historical synthetic observations. No live sensors or future failure horizon.

components.name: Keyboard focus treatment
components.description: Authored focus treatment on a semantic button; other geometry is framework-owned.

narrative.overview:
The user brief fixes a professional technical interface with navy and charcoal surfaces and restrained teal or blue accents. Mode: Operate. Primary tasks are locating observations, distinguishing recorded labels from model scores, and running inference. Flat analytical content and native Streamlit controls carry the interface.

This record preserves the existing sidebar, wide workspace, responsive stacking and explicit uncertainty. Values are extracted from .streamlit/config.toml and src/ui.py. No decorative imagery or authored animation appears in the implementation.
keyCharacteristics: Plain page titles and concise task descriptions.
Measurements with explicit units and labeled states.
Persistent desktop navigation and collapsible mobile navigation.
Analytical charts, tables and provenance caveats.

rules.name: The Readable Caveat Rule
rules.body: Captions use their explicit text color at full opacity. The original framework dimming reduced essential caveat contrast and is not part of the system.

dos: Do preserve the user's navy/charcoal technical direction and restrained accents.
Do keep measured labels, model scores, partitions and units explicit.
Do retain readable captions, native keyboard access and narrow-screen stacking.
Do substantiate analytics with real tables, charts and downloadable data.
donts: Don't communicate observed failure or risk category through color alone.
Don't present historical observations as live sensors or unique machines.
Don't style an uncalibrated score as a guaranteed probability or safety standard.
Don't invent radius, shadow, motion or typography scales absent from the implementation.
